test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution:
The correct answer is '**tallest**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage compares the Statue of Unity to other statues globally, emphasizing that it stands at the top in terms of height.
 
• "Tallest" is the superlative form of the adjective "tall", indicating that the Statue of Unity is the highest statue in the world.
 
• "**Tallest**" properly conveys the intended meaning of being the most tall among all statues.
 
• Other options ("**tall**", "**most tallest**", "**taller**") do not fit correctly. "Tall" and "taller" are not superlatives, and "most tallest" is grammatically incorrect as it redundantly repeats the superlative form.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The Statue of Unity, a towering tribute to India's Iron Man, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, situated__ on the banks of the majestic Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat's Kevadia, has __witnessed__ a remarkable surge in its annual footfall. In less than five years __since__ its inauguration, this colossal monument has welcomed nearly 16 crore visitors. In the first two months after the monument's inauguration in 2018, the world's __tallest__ statue witnessed a whopping 453,020 visitors followed by over 2.7 crore visitors in 2019. Even in 2020, the year tourism sector was battered by a once-in-a-century pandemic and subsequent movement restrictions, nearly 1.3 crore tourists flocked to the Statue of Unity. While the country was still recovering from the Covid-19 pandemic, the Statue of Unity saw a footfall of over 3.4 crores.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Tall: "Tall" is the positive degree and not appropriate for comparing the height against other statues.
 
• Most Tallest: "Most Tallest" is incorrect because it redundantly uses both "most" and "tallest" to form the superlative.
 
• Taller: "Taller" is the comparative form and not appropriate for indicating the absolute highest among all statues.
